environment.allocation: The exact kernel uses fixed stack arrays. Harness fixture/output buffers are allocated outside timers.

method.single_input_timing: One nonconstant input repeated 16,384 times per sample; per-call median is a warm batch mean, not individually timed latency.
method.large_batch_timing: 16,384 fixture values evaluated once per sample. Ordinary/extrapolation inputs vary; extreme inputs repeat 16 curated cases.
method.timed_scope: Indirect function dispatch, black_box on inputs/output, arithmetic and writes to a preallocated output buffer.
method.excluded_scope: Fixtures, oracles, validation, compilation, printing, graph scheduling, scripts, GUI and downstream error conversion.
method.clock: std::time::Instant wall time in integer nanoseconds
method.statistics: Median is sorted sample 5 of 9. One-process, fixed-order, descriptive microbenchmark; no confidence interval or application-wide inference.
method.order: For each workload and size, weighted first and exact second. No new FMA candidate or optimization was introduced.
method.concurrency: Other build/measurement work was paused for the short run. Shared-host noise was not otherwise controlled.

weighted_a1ffa400.formula: if t==0 {a} else if t==1 {b} else {(1-t)*a+t*b}
weighted_a1ffa400.contract: Historical separately rounded weighted products/addition, with endpoint preservation.

exact_fixed_point.formula: Round exact a+t*b-t*a once after fixed-point accumulation.
exact_fixed_point.contract: Nearest/even; preserve endpoint/identical-bit constants; negative nonzero underflow is -0; exact cancellation is +0; rounded overflow is signed infinity.

ordinary_0_to_1.oracle: Integer numerator (1024*ai+bi*ti)/1024. Its small integer numerator and power-of-two division are exactly representable.
ordinary_0_to_1.note: The large batch includes endpoint and equal-endpoint inputs; the selected single input is nonconstant.

extreme_finite_inputs.oracle: Python Fraction(a)+Fraction(t)*Fraction(b)-Fraction(t)*Fraction(a), converted once to binary64; apply endpoint/identical-bit rules and +0 cancellation. OverflowError maps to signed infinity.
extreme_finite_inputs.overflow_scope: All inputs are finite. Some expected outputs are infinity, valid for this kernel contract. Production callers reject nonfinite outputs; error-conversion cost is not measured.

fixture_selection_note: A preliminary ordinary single-input index selected a=b and therefore timed the constant shortcut. The final index is 124, with distinct a=-21,b=-20.75,t=0.484375. Only this final complete run is used for the cost report.

findings: Exact arithmetic passed every recorded check. Nonconstant ordinary/extrapolation/extreme single-input medians were approximately 134/129/125 ns per call.
For 16,384 values, exact median time was 1.948 ms for ordinary interpolation, 2.114 ms for extrapolation and 1.882 ms for the extreme mixture.
Historical weighted arithmetic costs about 2-4 ns per call in this harness. Exact arithmetic has a measurable cost and is selected for correctness, not speed.
The weighted extreme batch failed exact output-bit checks. Its timing remains visible but is excluded from ratios.
Warm batch means do not measure individual request latency, graph evaluation, Rhai execution or frame time.

At the stated 16,384-item limit these three local kernel batches cost about 2 ms on this host. This does not include graph evaluation, UI rendering or downstream errors and is not a measured graph/UI latency guarantee.

steps: Verify src/number_interpolation.rs against source.sha256. Create a private temporary directory.
Save harness_source as benchmark.rs after replacing __NODES_REPOSITORY__ with the absolute checkout path. Expected extreme bits are embedded; executing the harness needs only Rust std.
Run rustc --edition 2024 -O -C debuginfo=0 benchmark.rs -o benchmark. No Cargo target is added or built.
Pin to the same permitted CPU and run benchmark; on this Linux host taskset -c 0 ./benchmark is equivalent.
Parse the 12 JSON lines. Sort each nine duration_ns_per_sample values and take index 4. Divide by calls_per_sample for ns/call; multiply by logical_batch_size/1000 for microseconds per logical batch.
Retain mismatch counts and bit patterns. Report timing ratios only when both methods satisfy the same independent numerical oracle.
